title: Transcriptome-wide profiling of RNA G-quadruplex structures using rG4-seq
protocol: Culture authenticated human HeLa cells in DMEM media supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum.
Wash the cells (70-80% confluence) with Phosphate-buffered saline.
Detach the cells from surface using trypsin-EDTA.
Inactivate Trypsin by adding DMEM media supplemented with 10% FBS.
Pellet the suspended cells and extract total RNA using Qiagen RNeasy Plus Mini Kit.
Remove genomic DNA during RNA extraction process using gDNA eliminator columns provided in the kit.
Use 300 μg of total RNA per polyA purist kit reaction following manufacturer’s protocol.
Check the polyadenylated-enriched RNA with Agilent 2200 tapestation for reduction of rRNA peak as compared to total RNA input.
Perform RNA random fragmentation in 40 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.2, 100 mM LiCl, 30 mM MgCl₂ at 95°C for 90 s to yield average fragment size of ~250 nucleotides.
Clean and concentrate the fragmented RNA using RNA clean and concentrator according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Check the RNA with tapestation to determine the size of the fragmented RNA.
Perform 3’ dephosphorylation using 8 μl sample, 1 μl 10× T4 PNK buffer, 1 μl T4 PNK enzyme with no ATP added at 37°C for 30 min.
Conduct 3’adapter ligation by adding 10 μl sample from above, 1 μl of 50 μM 3’rApp adapter, 1 μl 10× T4 RNA ligase buffer, 6 μl PEG8000, and 2 μl T4 RNA ligase 2 K227Q at 25°C for an hour.
Use RNA clean and concentrator according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Divide the sample into three parts (10 μl each) for 150 mM Li+, 150 mM K+, and 150 mM K++ 5 μM PDS conditions for reverse transcription.
Add 1 μl of 10 μM unlabelled reverse primer, and 6 μl of 5× reverse transcription reaction buffer (final conc. 20 mM Tris, pH 7.5, 4 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM DTT, 0.5 mM dNTPs, 150 mM LiCl or 150 mM KCl).
Heat the mixture at 95°C for 1.5 min and cool it at 4°C for 1.5 min, then 37°C for 15 min for system equilibration.
At the beginning of the 37°C incubation, add 2 μl of nuclease-free water or 50 μM of PDS to the reaction and mix thoroughly.
After the 15 min incubation, add 1 μl of Superscript III (200U/μL) and carry out the reverse transcription at 37°C for 50 min.
Add 1 μl of 2M NaOH and degrade RNA at 95°C for 10 min.
Purify the cDNAs by 10% denaturing TBE gel and collect the size ~35-500nt.
Crush and soak the gel in 1×TEN250.
Incubate the gel at 80°C for 30 minutes.
Follow the manufacturer’s protocol to use RNA clean and concentrator.
Add 1 μl of 50 μM 5’adapter to the purified cDNAs (8 μl).
Heat the sample at 95°C for 3 min, then cool it to room temperature.
Add 10 μl of 2× Quick T4 ligase buffer and 1 μl Quick T4 DNA ligase to the sample.
Incubate the sample at 20°C overnight.
Purify the ligated cDNAs by running them on a 10% denaturing TBE gel.
Obtain size-selected fragments of 75-500 nt from the gel and extract them.
Perform PCR reaction (25 μl) using the specified conditions and primers, including forward primer and reverse primer.
Purify the amplified libraries with a 1.8% agarose gel.
Extract DNA libraries using Genejet gel extraction kit following manufacturer’s protocol.
Perform qPCR on purified libraries with KAPA Universal Quant Kit.
Pool the libraries according to qPCR results.
Submit the pooled libraries for next generation sequencing on NextSeq500 machine for a single 1 × 150 bp cycle run.
Trim fastq files generated by sequencing for removal of Illumina adapters and low quality tails using trim galore software.
Align the trimmed data to the human reference genome version hg19 using tophat2 software.
Remove aligned reads with mapping quality below 30 using samtools.
Calculate coverage bedGraph files using exon features merged by gene as interval file with bedtools.
Load coverage files for processing in R.
Convolve the coverage signal with a step-like filter of order 10 to highlight drops in signal at each base using an R function filter.
Convolve the coverage signal with a different step-like filter of order 10 to normalize for total coverage upstream of each base using an R function filter.
Calculate the ratio of the two convolved signals for each base, yielding a normalized convolved signal between -1 and 1.
Identify positive or negative values indicating an increase or decrease in coverage at each base.
Assign a value of 1 to indicate a full drop in coverage from n to 0.
Determine local maxima of the normalized convolved signal to identify genomic locations with pronounced coverage drops.
Calculate reverse transcriptase stalling (RTS) values for these identified local maxima.
Exclude bases with single-base coverage below 6 and RTS below 0.2 from analysis.
Select two conditions, such as K+ and Li+, and use their normalized convolved coverage signals to fit a linear model.
Estimate the p-value of the fitting using ANOVA testing through the function lm in R.
Correct all p-values from the linear models contrasting any two conditions for multiple hypothesis testing by applying FDR correction on all tested local maxima.
Identify significant regions as those having FDR ≤ 0.1 and refer to them as scoring regions, or “RTS sites”, yielding a value in the range 0-1, where 0 indicates no stalling and 1 full stalling.
Remove sites with RTS value < 0.25 from the analysis to further remove regions with subtle effects.
Convert the genomic coordinates of RTS regions to transcript coordinates.
Calculate FPKM for each transcript isoform in the Li+ condition using the software cufflinks, considering transcripts with FPKM ≥ 0.5 as expressed.
Map genomic scoring regions to exons belonging to the transcript with highest FPKM among the expressed ones for each given gene.
If the genomic coordinates fall into intronic regions, assess the second most expressed transcript and so on.
Calculate transcript coordinates and sequence for the mapped scoring regions to account for intron skipping.
Extract sequences extending from the RTS stalling site to 50 base pairs upstream in the transcript for each RTS site.
Assign extracted sequences to different rG4s structural sub-classes based on defined criteria.
Classify G3L1-7 as canonical rG4s with loop length between 1-7nt using regular expressions.
Identify long-loops as rG4s with any loop of length >7nt, up to 12 nt for lateral loops and 21 for the central loop.
Categorize bulges as rG4s with a bulge of 1–7nt in one G-tract or multiple 1nt bulges.
Classify 2-quartet as rG4s with 4-tracts of two consecutive Gs.
Assign sequences containing more than 40% G-content to the G≥40% category if they do not fit into previous categories.
When matching multiple categories, assign a region to the class with higher predicted stability from first to last: canonical rG4s, long loops, bulges, 2-quartet.
Extract exonic canonical rG4s (category G3L1-7) with coverage ≥ 20 in the Li+ condition.
Equally extend each rG4 sequence upstream and downstream to enclose a total region of 90 nt including both the rG4 motif and flanking regions.
Count the occurrence of C, CC, CCC, and CCCC motifs within each extended region containing detected or undetected rG4s.
Divide the motif counts by the region length to yield a motif density value per sequence.
Similarly, count the occurrence of U, A, and G motifs within each extended region.
Compute the average value of detected and undetected G3L1-7 density.
Calculate the ratio of the average detected to average undetected density.
For each G3L1-7 identified in step 47., equally extend upstream and downstream by 45 nucleotides to enclose a total region of 90nt.
Calculate the free energy of ensemble of these sequences using RNAFold software of the ViennaRNA package.
Compare the free energy values for detected and undetected G3L1-7 regions.
Calculate the overlap of each scoring region with 5’UTR, CDS, and 3’UTR using bedtools intersect.
Assign rG4s partially overlapping multiple regions to both regions and count twice.
Divide the number of overlapping regions to each annotated feature by the total region size in base pairs.
Multiply the result by 1000 to yield the rG4 density per kilobase.
Normalize each transcript profile to the same length.
Divide the 5’UTR, CDS and 3’UTR into 5, 40 and 40 bins respectively.
Assess the belonging of each RTS site to a given bin.
Compute 1/bin_size for count normalization by bin size in bp.
Average all normalized counts per bin for scored regions in all transcripts.
Plot the average values obtained from step 8.
Obtain microRNA target sites from TargetScan database.
Obtain polyadenylation signal (PAS) sites from GENCODE project.
Transform genomic coordinates of all sites into transcript coordinates.
Calculate distance between the region and closest feature, skipping introns.
Assign 0 for overlapping features.
Randomly shuffle scoring regions by uniform resampling across all expressed transcripts after merging overlapping exons.
Build cumulative distributions of pairwise feature-region distances for RTS sites and random regions.
Assess cumulative distribution of distance separately for rG4s up- and downstream of the respective regulatory sites.
Calculate the fraction of rG4s in proximity (i.e., ≤100 nt) of regulatory sites for all rG4s and for up- and downstream rG4s, and compare to random by using the Chi-squared test for proportions.
Extract unique sequences only from scoring regions (RTS sites).
Consider overlapping rG4s identified as single rG4s if the G-quadruplex motif coincides through hierarchical motif analysis.
Extend 50 nt scoring regions by 100nt up- and downstream, resulting in regions of 250 nt.
Use RNAFold software for structural prediction of the 250 nt sequences.
Repeat the structural prediction with and without imposing single-strand constraint over the rG4 identified motif.
Impose the single-strand constraint over the G-quadruplex motif closer to the identified stalling site.
Use RNAstructure software to convert dot bracket (db) files to connectivity table (ct) files.
Perform structure comparison between constrained and unconstrained structural predictions using CircleCompare function of RNAstructure.
Calculate the positive predictive value (PPV) returned by CircleCompare for structure comparisons.
Survey the presence of orthologous genes in 68 non-human eukaryotic species from the Ensembl genome database via BioMart.
Perform a global sequence alignment between human and non-human cDNA sequences using the Biostrings library for R.
Use substitution matrix parameters matching the default options of blastn aligner: match = 2, mismatch = -3, gap opening = 5, gap extension = 2.
Identify the rG4h sequence in the aligned human cDNA by considering +10 downstream and -50 upstream sequences from the rG4-seq revealed coordinate of the 3'-end of rG4h.
Correct the identified rG4 coordinates to account for gaps introduced in the alignment.
Examine the matched segment from the aligned non-human cDNAnon-h sequence corresponding to the region in human cDNAh that engulfs the particular rG4h sequence.
Remove gaps from the examined segment if introduced during alignment.
Assess the presence of a potential G-quadruplex using the relaxed (G2+N1-12)3G2+ sequence pattern.
Identify G4 sequences that match with the actual experimentally validated rG4h by their positioning inside the orthologs.

Store the outcome in a matrix (N rG4s × 69 species), with 1 if there is a rG4, 0 if an ortholog is found but without a G4 sequence at the matching locus, and NA for cases where even an ortholog is absent.
Use the matrix to cluster data entries in both rG4 and species dimensions.
Produce a heatmap where the G4 presence patterns are clustered.
